metadata.source: Curated from central labour acts, Labour Codes, and major state Shops & Establishments Acts. Implementation status as of June 2026. Always verify with latest central/state notifications.
metadata.disclaimer: This is a curated knowledge base for informational use only. It is not legal advice. Labour law changes frequently at state level.

entries.title: Definition of retrenchment and conditions precedent to retrenchment
entries.summary: Retrenchment means termination of service for any reason whatsoever, otherwise than as a punishment inflicted by way of disciplinary action. For workmen with 1+ year continuous service, employer must give 1 month notice or pay in lieu, and compensation of 15 days average pay for every completed year.

applicability.company_size: Any (special rules apply for establishments with 100+ workmen under Chapter VB in some states)

entries.title: Procedure for retrenchment
entries.summary: The employer shall ordinarily retrench the workman who was the last person to be employed in that category. This is the 'last come first go' principle.

entries.title: Time of payment of wages
entries.summary: Wages must be paid before the expiry of the 7th day after the last day of the wage period. For establishments with 1000+ employees, before the 10th day.

employee_types: All employees drawing wages below the ceiling (currently ₹24,000/month in most states)

entries.title: Payment of minimum rates of wages
entries.summary: Employer shall pay to every employee engaged in a scheduled employment wages at a rate not less than the minimum rate of wages fixed by the appropriate government.

states: All India (central act) - rates fixed by State Governments

entries.title: Payment of minimum bonus
entries.summary: Every employer shall pay to every employee a minimum bonus of 8.33% of the salary or wage earned by the employee during the accounting year or ₹100, whichever is higher.

employee_types: Employees drawing salary up to ₹21,000 per month

entries.title: Payment of gratuity
entries.summary: Gratuity is payable to an employee on termination of employment after continuous service of 5 years. Rate is 15 days wages for every completed year of service. No minimum service required in case of death or disablement.

applicability.company_size: Every shop or establishment employing 10 or more persons

entries.act: Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
entries.title: Contributions
entries.summary: Employee contributes 12% of basic wages + DA + retaining allowance. Employer contributes 12% (3.67% to EPF + 8.33% to EPS).

employee_types: Employees earning up to ₹15,000 per month (can be higher voluntarily)

entries.title: Contributions
entries.summary: Employee contributes 0.75% of wages. Employer contributes 3.25% of wages. Covers medical benefit, sickness benefit, maternity benefit, disablement benefit, dependent benefit.

states: All India (central act) - implemented in notified areas
employee_types: Employees drawing wages up to ₹21,000 per month

entries.title: Right to payment of maternity benefit
entries.summary: Every woman is entitled to maternity benefit at the rate of the average daily wage for the period of her actual absence (maximum 26 weeks for first two children, 12 weeks for third and subsequent).

entries.act: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
entries.title: Duties of employer
entries.summary: Every employer must provide a safe working environment, constitute Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) where 10+ employees, display penal consequences, organize workshops, assist in filing complaint with police if required.

employee_types: Women employees (and men in some interpretations)
applicability.company_size: All workplaces (ICC mandatory for 10 or more employees)

entries.title: Registration of establishments
entries.summary: Principal employer must register the establishment if employing 20 or more contract labourers. Contractor must obtain licence.

entries.title: Weekly hours
entries.summary: No adult worker shall be required or allowed to work in a factory for more than 48 hours in any week.

entries.title: Minimum wages and floor wage
entries.summary: The Code subsumes Minimum Wages Act, Payment of Wages Act, Payment of Bonus Act and Equal Remuneration Act. Central government to fix national floor wage. States must fix minimum wages not less than floor wage. As of June 2026, full implementation status varies significantly by state.

states: Implementation status varies by state — check latest notification

entries.implementation_status: Partially notified in several states. Many provisions still governed by old acts in states that have not fully implemented the Code.

entries.title: Changes to termination rules for larger establishments
entries.summary: The Code raises the threshold for prior government permission for lay-off/retrenchment/closure from 100 to 300 workers in some cases. Standing orders now required for establishments with 300+ workers (earlier 100). Implementation status is uneven across states as of 2026.

states: Implementation status varies — many states have not yet notified corresponding rules

entries.implementation_status: Not uniformly implemented. Several states continue to apply pre-existing thresholds under old laws.

entries.title: Unified social security framework
entries.summary: Subsumes EPF Act, ESI Act, Payment of Gratuity Act, Maternity Benefit Act, and others. Introduces gig worker and platform worker definitions with social security provisions. Full operationalization is still in progress across states.
entries.implementation_status: Partial rollout. Core EPF/ESI/gratuity provisions largely continue under old acts in most jurisdictions until full state adoption.

entries.act: Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020
entries.title: Consolidated OSH framework
entries.summary: Subsumes Factories Act, Contract Labour Act, and several others. Introduces single registration, inter-state migrant worker provisions, and updated working hour rules. Implementation is gradual.
entries.implementation_status: Many states still operating under old Acts for factories, contract labour, and working conditions as of mid-2026.

entries.act: Maharashtra Shops and Establishments (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act, 2017
entries.title: Working hours, weekly holiday, leave
entries.summary: Maximum 9 hours per day and 48 hours per week. Employee entitled to one paid holiday per week. Earned leave: 1 day for every 20 days worked (max 27 days). Casual leave and sick leave also provided.

applicability.company_size: All (registration required based on employee count)

entries.act: Delhi Shops and Establishments Act, 1954 (as amended)
entries.title: Hours of work and holidays
entries.summary: No employee shall be required to work more than 9 hours in a day or 48 hours in a week. One whole day holiday in a week with wages.

entries.act: Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1961
entries.title: Daily and weekly hours
entries.summary: Maximum 9 hours a day and 48 hours a week. Overtime permitted with double wages.

employee_types: Employees in shops and commercial establishments

entries.source: Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishments Act

entries.act: General Principles (cross-referenced across ID Act + state S&E Acts)
entries.title: Termination without cause for non-workmen / managerial staff
entries.summary: For employees not classified as 'workmen' under the Industrial Disputes Act (typically managers, supervisors above certain salary), employment contracts and state Shops & Establishments Acts govern notice period. Common practice is 30-90 days notice or pay in lieu. No automatic retrenchment compensation unless contract provides.
entries.source: General employment law principles + state S&E Acts

entries.title: Advance from PF account
entries.summary: Members can withdraw up to 50% of PF balance for marriage, education, illness, or purchase of site/house after 7 years membership. Full withdrawal allowed on retirement after 58 or on leaving service after 2 months of unemployment.

entries.act: State Shops & Establishments Acts + Factories Act
entries.title: Earned leave, casual leave, sick leave
entries.summary: Most states provide 12-15 days casual/sick leave and 15-21 days earned/privilege leave per year. Exact entitlements differ by state Shops & Establishments Act and whether the establishment is a factory.

states: Varies by state — always check local S&E Act

entries.act: Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946 / IR Code
entries.title: Applicability of standing orders
entries.summary: Industrial establishments with 100 or more workmen (threshold raised to 300 in some states under new Code) must have certified standing orders covering classification of workers, shift working, attendance, leave, termination, etc.

applicability.company_size: 100+ (or 300+ in states that adopted new Code)
